title: Find the Pattern
statement:
Given a text `s` and a pattern `p` (lowercase letters only), count how many times `p` occurs in `s` as a contiguous substring. Occurrences may overlap.

**Input.** Two lines: `s`, then `p`.

**Output.** Two lines: the number of occurrences, then the 0-based start index of the first occurrence (or `-1` if there is none).
constraints: both strings consist of lowercase letters `a` to `z`
hints: Checking every start position and comparing character by character is O(|s|·|p|), which is far too slow when both are 10^5 long and almost all characters match.

After a mismatch you already know the last few text characters. The longest proper prefix of the pattern that is also a suffix of what you matched tells you where to resume without moving backwards in the text.

Build pi[i] = length of the longest proper border of p[:i+1]. Scan the text with a counter k of matched characters; on a mismatch set k = pi[k-1] until it matches or hits 0. After a full match (k == |p|) the same fallback lets overlapping matches be found.
editorial: KMP precomputes the prefix function `pi` of the pattern in `O(|p|)`: `pi[i]` is the length of the longest proper prefix of `p[:i+1]` that is also its suffix. Scanning the text, keep `k`, the length of the current match. On a mismatch, `k` falls back to `pi[k-1]`; the text pointer never moves backwards. The total number of fallbacks is bounded by the total number of increments (an amortized argument like the monotonic stack), so the scan is `O(|s|)`. After a full match, falling back with `pi` lets overlapping occurrences be counted. Hashing is an alternative but can collide; KMP is deterministic.

starter.python:
import sys
s, p = sys.stdin.read().split()
# print the number of occurrences, then the first index (or -1)
